title: Maximum Points Tourist Can Earn
summary: Given the integers n and k, along with two 2D integer arrays stayScore and travelScore, a tourist visits n cities over k days.
statement: Given the integers n and k, along with two 2D integer arrays stayScore and travelScore, a tourist visits n cities over k days. Each day, the tourist can either stay in their current city and earn points as specified in the stayScore array, or travel to another city and earn points as specified in the travelScore array. The objective is to determine the maximum total points the tourist can earn over the k days.
constraints: There are 1–200 cities and exactly 1–200 days; the tourist may start in any city.
Staying on day d in city c earns stay_score[d][c]; moving from origin to a different destination earns travel_score[origin][destination].
Return the maximum total over all valid city routes.
hints: The only history needed after a day is the best score ending in each city.
For every destination, try staying from itself or traveling from every other origin.
Initialize every possible start at zero; repeat k destination transitions; return the best endpoint.
Each route has one previous endpoint, so the transition considers every route exactly through its best prefix.
editorial: Each route has one previous endpoint, so the transition considers every route exactly through its best prefix.

tests.explanation: Starting in city 1 and staying earns three, better than either move.
Stay in city 1 for four points, then move to city 2 for four more.
